name: The Spread — arrival, with a writing station first
note: The answer to 'what is the first thing you would need to do', and it inverts the Hellenic board rather than reskinning it. There, records comes AFTER trade: cuneiform begins as barley tallies, the ledger is downstream of the exchange, and the first thing anybody wrote was a receipt for something that already had a market. That is true when you GROW a surplus from nothing. It is false when you ARRIVE with one. Land with a forest and colonists and the very first thing you need is a writing station, because you already have a spread and nobody knows what is in it, who brought it, or what is owed on it — and every allocation you make before that is a guess you cannot audit later. So here the record is a root and almost everything hangs off it. Same twelve sectors, same twelve names, opposite build order, and the difference is entirely in what you were handed on day one.

sectors.name: The writing station
sectors.why: First, and it is first because you arrived with things. A tally of what is in the spread, who carried it, and what is owed on it. Every allocation made before this one is a guess you cannot audit afterwards, and the whole reason writing exists is that somebody had a heap and needed to say how big it was without moving it.

sectors.name: The forest
sectors.why: You have it. That is the difference between this board and the other one — the commons is not something you protect on the way to building an economy, it is the asset you landed on top of, and it starts full and only goes one way unless somebody spends a window on it.

sectors.name: The colonists
sectors.why: They came with you and they need an address before they need anything else. A root here for the same reason it is a root anywhere, except that on this board the people exist before the shelter does, which is the wrong way round and is exactly the pressure you are under.

sectors.name: Stores
sectors.why: Not grown — counted. The food came off the ship and the only question is how long it lasts, which is a question the writing station answers and nothing else can. Rationing without a tally is not rationing, it is hoping.

sectors.name: Water
sectors.why: Downstream of the record here, which looks wrong until you notice you are siting a waterway inside a forest that already exists. You are not choosing where the water goes; you are finding out where it already is and writing it down.

sectors.name: Standing
sectors.why: Who is owed what, binding past the moment of saying it. It arrives early on this board and late on the other one, and the reason is the same reason: an oath needs a record, and here the record was the first thing built.

sectors.name: Want
sectors.why: A root on the Hellenic board and not one here, which is the sharpest single difference between them. When you arrive with stores, nobody wants anything for a while — demand appears the moment the counted pile visibly stops being enough, and not one day before.

sectors.name: Skill
sectors.why: Teaching is a day not spent doing, which is affordable only once somebody can say whose day it was. Downstream of standing rather than of food, because on this board the constraint is not calories, it is who is entitled to spend the hour.

sectors.name: Exchange
sectors.why: Needs somebody to want something and a way to bind the deal. Late here, and it is the node that shows the inversion most plainly: on the Hellenic board trade comes before the ledger and here it comes two ranks after it.

sectors.name: Forge
sectors.why: Tools that make tools, and it needs both a market to be worth supplying and water to work with. The first thing on this board that could not have come off the ship.

sectors.name: Force
sectors.why: Downstream of the exchange, because force needs something worth taking and a spread nobody trades is a spread nobody has priced. A settlement that budgets security before it has a market has described a garrison.

sectors.name: Appeal
sectors.why: The last resort, and it still cannot come first. It needs the binding and it needs somebody trained to read it — a rule with nobody able to interpret it is authority ruling by memory, which is the failure this node exists to prevent on either board.
